# Colour grading Frame Job grades a clip from the inspector's **Color** tab. You can set exposure and white balance, push the shadows, midtones and highlights toward a colour with three wheels, shape tones and hues with curves, and finish with one of eight built-in looks or your own `.cube` LUT. An **adjustment clip** grades everything behind it at once, and its **qualifier** can narrow that grade to one colour or tone range. To check your work, **Show Ungraded** gives a before/after view and **Scopes** shows a waveform, parade, vectorscope and histogram beside the preview. Every grade setting can be animated in an action. The preview, **Save Frame…** and every export draw a grade the same way. A clip you haven't graded renders exactly as it would without one. ## The Color tab Select one or more clips and open the inspector's **Clip** tab. The **Color** sub-tab appears when every selected clip can take a grade: - a video clip, an image clip or a still (freeze frame), or - an adjustment clip. It does not appear for text, shape, graphic or nest clips, and a selection of nothing but audio-only clips has no Color tab. Mixing in a text, shape, graphic or nest clip hides the tab. An audio-only clip selected alongside a video clip does not hide it; the grade goes only to the clips that draw. The tab's sections, from top to bottom: | Section | Shown for | |---|---| | Adjustment | Adjustment clips only (every selected clip must be one) | | Qualifier | Adjustment clips only (every selected clip must be one) | | Light | Every gradable clip | | Color | Every gradable clip | | Wheels | Every gradable clip | | Curves | Every gradable clip | | Look | Every gradable clip | Each section's header shows a short summary, such as "neutral", "adjusted", "Warm 80%" or "hue · sat · inverted", and has a **Reset** button that returns only that section to neutral. If no section is open, the tab opens the first one you haven't closed yourself. **Working on several clips.** A control writes only the setting it governs. Dragging Exposure across three clips changes their exposure and leaves each clip's other values alone. When the selected clips have different values, the row shows a mixed badge. **Undo.** Dragging a slider is one undo step, and so is a typed value. Each step is named after its control, for example **Undo Exposure**, **Undo Hue** or **Undo Strength**. A section's **Reset** is one step named after the section ("Light", "Color", "Look", "Adjustment", "Qualifier"). The order the grade is applied in is fixed: Color first, then Light, Wheels, Curves (tone curves, then the hue curves) and the Look. The clip's filters from the Picture tab's **Filters** section split around the grade: Pixelate, Blur and Sharpen act on the picture before it, and Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert act after the Look, in the order of their slots. That matters when you combine a filter such as Noir or Vignette with a grade. A camera-log conversion set on the media comes before all of them (see [HDR and colour management](hdr-and-color.md)). ## Wheels **Wheels** shows three columns side by side, **Lift**, **Gamma** and **Gain**: - **Lift** moves black and holds white, so it mostly affects the shadows. - **Gamma** moves the middle tones and holds both ends. - **Gain** moves white and holds black, so it mostly affects the highlights. Each column has a colour disc, a strip under it, and a number field. Hover a disc to see its push as a tooltip, such as "Hue 34° · 0.25" (the hue angle and the strength), or "Neutral" when the puck is centred. There is no number field for the push itself. **The disc** pushes its tonal range toward a colour. The puck's direction picks the hue and its distance from the centre sets the strength. The disc is turned to match the vectorscope, so dragging toward a colour moves the vectorscope trace toward it. - Press anywhere on the disc and drag. The puck moves by however far the pointer moves; it doesn't jump to where you clicked. Dragging one disc radius gives the full push. - Hold ⌥ to move at a tenth of the speed. - Past the rim, the puck slides along the rim. - Double-click the disc to reset the push to the centre. This leaves the wheel's brightness alone. **The strip and the field** set the wheel's master brightness, from −1 to +1 (two decimals in the field): - Click off the knob to jump the value there, or drag the knob from where it stands. - Hold ⌥ to drag at a tenth of the speed, relative to where you started. - Double-click the strip to reset the master to 0. This is one undo step, even when the first click of the double-click moved the knob. Each drag is one undo step, named after its wheel. **Reset** sets all three wheels back to neutral. *Agents:* `set_video` with `wheels: {lift, gamma, gain}`, each `{x, y, master}` from −1 to 1. The point `(x, y)` must lie inside the unit circle, and its angle is the hue, with red at 0°. ## Curves ## Grading inside an action Every grade setting can be animated. Select an action on the clip's action lane, then change a control. The change goes to the action's end state, and the value ramps there from the clip's own value. The row marks (◆) and the Color tab's badge show which settings the selected action animates. See [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md) for actions. - **Light, Color, wheels, Strength, the look's Amount and the qualifier's numbers** ramp smoothly. An animated hue centre takes the short way round the colour wheel; 350° to 10° passes through 0°. - **Curves** animate between any two curves, even with different numbers of points, and from or to a straight line. Inside an action, a channel cell's **Reset Red** (or whichever channel) and the row's **Set end value to default** write a straight curve to the action's end, so the curve animates back to neutral. - **Turning a look on or off, or changing it, applies to the clip itself, not to the action**, even with an action selected. A look that differs between start and end switches at the action's end. Amount is what animates. - **Turning a qualifier range on or off** switches at the action's end. While an action is selected, a grade section's header shows **Clear** in place of **Reset**, and only when the action animates one of that section's rows: it removes the section's settings from the action. Right-click a grade row for **Remove from action N** or **Set end value to default**. The grade controls show the action's animation in their own way: - **Wheel disc:** a hollow square at the action's start value, the puck in action colour, and a coral mark at the value under the playhead. - **Wheel strip:** filled in action colour from the start value, with a coral tick at the playhead's value. - **Curve plot:** the action's start curve dashed, and the edited curve and its points in action colour. - **Qualifier strip:** the band outlined and its knobs drawn in action colour. Sliders carry the same marks as everywhere else in the inspector; see [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md). *Agents:* `add_action`, then `set_action_end` with a `video` patch carrying `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look.amount` or `qualifier`. ## Copying a grade: Paste Attributes Copy a graded clip (⌘C), select other clips, and choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (⌥⌘V). The copied clip's video settings replace each selected clip's in one undo step: its grade, look, filters and the rest of its picture settings, including position and scale. Where the copied clip has sound, its audio settings come too. A clip's place, speed, actions, transitions, name and label are never copied. Qualifiers follow the clip type: - Pasting onto an ordinary clip drops the qualifier. - Pasting from an ordinary clip onto an adjustment clip keeps the adjustment clip's own qualifier. - Between two adjustment clips, the qualifier is copied. Pasting a clip that has blur, sharpen, pixelate or a blend mode onto an adjustment clip is refused. *Agents:* `paste_attributes`, which takes `groups` (`video`, `audio`, `text`, `shape`, `graphic`) to copy only some of them. ## Limits - The Color tab needs every selected clip to be gradable. Deselect text, shape, graphic and nest clips first. - Qualifiers exist only on adjustment clips. To grade one colour, put an adjustment clip above the picture for the span you want. It grades every track behind it, so a matte track cutting its track is how you confine it to one area (see [Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md)). - There is no Offset wheel. Use Color's **Brightness** for an overall lift. - Show Ungraded, Show Selection and the scopes affect only the window's preview. Nothing about them is saved or exported. - A curve holds at most 16 points and at least 2. - Only 3D `.cube` LUTs with a size of 2 to 65 are read. ---
title: "Wheels"
description: "Balance a clip's shadows, middle tones and highlights with Lift, Gamma and Gain, pushing each toward a colour and setting its brightness."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The wheels balance a picture by tone. **Lift** works on the shadows, **Gamma** on the middle tones and **Gain** on the highlights, so you can cool the shadows, warm the highlights or take a colour cast out of one part of the picture without touching the rest.

<AtAGlance
  keys={['⌥-drag', 'Double-click']}
  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Wheels"
  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
/>

<Shot
  name="05f-clip-wheels.inspector"
  alt="The Wheels section of the Color tab, reading adjusted, with a Reset button. Three columns, Lift, Gamma and Gain, each hold a colour disc, a strip and a number field. Lift's puck is pushed up and to the left, toward red-orange, and its field reads 0.10. Gamma is centred at 0.00. Gain's puck is centred and its field reads 0.20."
/>

## The Wheels section

<Steps>

1. Select a video clip, an image, a still or an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/). An adjustment clip's wheels grade everything behind it.

2. Open the **Color** tab in the Clip inspector. See [The Color tab](/color/color-tab/) for which clips have it.

3. Open **Wheels**. It starts closed, and its header reads **neutral** until a wheel moves, then **adjusted**.

</Steps>

Each of the three columns has a colour disc for the [push](#push-a-range-toward-a-colour), and a strip and a number field for its [brightness](#set-a-wheels-brightness). Every value starts at 0, which leaves the picture unchanged.

The wheels apply after **Color** and **Light**, and before the [curves](/color/curves/) and the [look](/color/looks/). Their order is fixed.

## What each wheel moves

| Wheel | What it moves | Brightness at +1 | Brightness at −1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Lift** | Moves black and holds white, so it mostly affects the shadows. | Black rises to 25 %. | Everything below 20 % goes to black. |
| **Gamma** | Moves the middle tones and holds both ends. | A 50 % grey rises to about 71 %. | A 50 % grey falls to 25 %. |
| **Gain** | Moves white and holds black, so it mostly affects the highlights. | Every level is multiplied by 1.5. | Every level is halved, so white falls to 50 %. |

A push follows the same rule. On **Lift** it tints the blacks and leaves white alone, and on **Gain** it tints the whites and leaves black alone.

## Push a range toward a colour

Press anywhere on a disc and drag. The direction you drag picks the hue, and the distance from the centre sets the strength.

The square puck moves by however far the pointer moves. It doesn't jump to where you pressed, and a press with no drag changes nothing. Dragging one disc radius gives the full push, and past the rim the puck slides along the rim.

A puck changes only that wheel's colour, never its brightness. One drag is one undo step, named after the wheel, such as **Undo Lift**.

## Set a wheel's brightness

The strip and the field under each disc set that wheel's master brightness, from −1 to +1. The default is 0.

- **Click the strip** off the knob and the value jumps there.
- **Drag the knob** and it moves from where it stands, with no jump.
- **Type in the field** for an exact value. It shows two decimals and has no unit. Return, Tab or a click elsewhere saves it, and <kbd>Esc</kbd> keeps the old value. A number past either end is set to −1 or 1, and anything that isn't a number is ignored.

A drag is one undo step and so is a typed value, each named after its wheel.

## Make a fine adjustment

Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag a puck or a strip to move at a tenth of the speed. On a strip, a press with <kbd>⌥</kbd> held moves the value relative to where it stands, with no jump.

On a disc you can press or let go of <kbd>⌥</kbd> at any point in a drag. On a strip, letting go of <kbd>⌥</kbd> before the mouse sends the knob back under the pointer.

The same key slows a point on a [curve](/color/curves/) and a handle on a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/).

## Read the push

Hover a disc to see its push as a hue angle and a strength, such as **Hue 34° · 0.25**. A centred puck reads **Neutral**.

The angle counts from red at 0°, with green at 120° and blue at 240°. The strength runs from 0 at the centre to 1 at the rim. The push has no number field, so this is the only place to read it.

## Wheels match the vectorscope

Each disc is turned so that a hue sits where the [vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/) draws it. Dragging toward a colour moves the trace toward that colour.

Red sits 103° counter-clockwise from 3 o'clock, just left of the top. Going counter-clockwise from there you'll find yellow on the left, green at the lower left, cyan near the bottom, blue on the right and magenta at the upper right. Every 75 % target on the vectorscope falls within 12° of its place on the disc.

## Reset the wheels

| To reset | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| One wheel's push | Double-click its disc. The puck returns to the centre and the wheel's brightness stays. |
| One wheel's brightness | Double-click its strip. The value returns to 0 and the push stays. |
| All three wheels | Choose **Reset** in the section's header, or right-click the wheels and choose **Reset to default**. **Reset** appears once a wheel has moved. |

Each of these is one undo step. That holds even when the first click of a double-click on the strip moved the knob. **Reset** is named **Wheels** in the **Edit** menu.

## Grade several clips at once

Select the clips and use the wheels as usual. Each control writes only its own values. A puck gives every selected clip that wheel's push and leaves each clip's brightness and other wheels alone. A strip or a field does the same for that wheel's brightness.

The controls show the first clip's values. When the clips differ on any wheel, a **mixed** badge appears. One badge covers all three wheels.

## Animate the wheels

With an action selected, a puck, a strip or a field sets the action's end value, and the wheels ramp there from the clip's own values. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).

While the action animates the wheels, a disc shows a hollow square at the start value and the puck in the action colour. A strip fills in the action colour from the start value. A coral mark shows the value under the playhead when it differs.

The three wheels are one row, so they go in or out of an action together. Right-click them for **Remove from action N** or **Set end value to default**, or choose **Clear** in the section's header.

## Good to know

There's no Offset wheel. For an overall lift, use **Brightness** in the [Color section](/color/color-section/).

---
title: "Wheels"
description: "Balance a clip's shadows, middle tones and highlights with Lift, Gamma and Gain, pushing each toward a colour and setting its brightness."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The wheels balance a picture by tone. **Lift** works on the shadows, **Gamma** on the middle tones and **Gain** on the highlights, so you can cool the shadows, warm the highlights or take a colour cast out of one part of the picture without touching the rest.

<AtAGlance
  keys={['⌥-drag', 'Double-click']}
  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Wheels"
  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
/>

<Shot
  name="05f-clip-wheels.inspector"
  alt="The Wheels section of the Color tab, reading adjusted, with a Reset button. Three columns, Lift, Gamma and Gain, each hold a colour disc, a strip and a number field. Lift's puck is pushed up and to the left, toward red-orange, and its field reads 0.10. Gamma is centred at 0.00. Gain's puck is centred and its field reads 0.20."
/>

## The Wheels section

<Steps>

1. Select a video clip, an image, a still or an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/). An adjustment clip's wheels grade everything behind it.

2. Open the **Color** tab in the Clip inspector. See [The Color tab](/color/color-tab/) for which clips have it.

3. Open **Wheels**. It starts closed, and its header reads **neutral** until a wheel moves, then **adjusted**.

</Steps>

Each of the three columns has a colour disc for the [push](#push-a-range-toward-a-colour), and a strip and a number field for its [brightness](#set-a-wheels-brightness). Every value starts at 0, which leaves the picture unchanged.

The wheels apply after **Color** and **Light**, and before the [curves](/color/curves/) and the [look](/color/looks/). Their order is fixed.

## What each wheel moves

| Wheel | What it moves | Brightness at +1 | Brightness at −1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Lift** | Moves black and holds white, so it mostly affects the shadows. | Black rises to 25 %. | Everything below 20 % goes to black. |
| **Gamma** | Moves the middle tones and holds both ends. | A 50 % grey rises to about 71 %. | A 50 % grey falls to 25 %. |
| **Gain** | Moves white and holds black, so it mostly affects the highlights. | Every level is multiplied by 1.5. | Every level is halved, so white falls to 50 %. |

A push follows the same rule. On **Lift** it tints the blacks and leaves white alone, and on **Gain** it tints the whites and leaves black alone.

## Push a range toward a colour

Press anywhere on a disc and drag. The direction you drag picks the hue, and the distance from the centre sets the strength.

The square puck moves by however far the pointer moves. It doesn't jump to where you pressed, and a press with no drag changes nothing. Dragging one disc radius gives the full push, and past the rim the puck slides along the rim.

A puck changes only that wheel's colour, never its brightness. One drag is one undo step, named after the wheel, such as **Undo Lift**.

## Set a wheel's brightness

The strip and the field under each disc set that wheel's master brightness, from −1 to +1. The default is 0.

- **Click the strip** off the knob and the value jumps there.
- **Drag the knob** and it moves from where it stands, with no jump.
- **Type in the field** for an exact value. It shows two decimals and has no unit. Return, Tab or a click elsewhere saves it, and <kbd>Esc</kbd> keeps the old value. A number past either end is set to −1 or 1, and anything that isn't a number is ignored.

A drag is one undo step and so is a typed value, each named after its wheel.

## Make a fine adjustment

Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag a puck or a strip to move at a tenth of the speed. On a strip, a press with <kbd>⌥</kbd> held moves the value relative to where it stands, with no jump.

On a disc you can press or let go of <kbd>⌥</kbd> at any point in a drag. On a strip, letting go of <kbd>⌥</kbd> before the mouse sends the knob back under the pointer.

The same key slows a point on a [curve](/color/curves/) and a handle on a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/).

## Read the push

Hover a disc to see its push as a hue angle and a strength, such as **Hue 34° · 0.25**. A centred puck reads **Neutral**.

The angle counts from red at 0°, with green at 120° and blue at 240°. The strength runs from 0 at the centre to 1 at the rim. The push has no number field, so this is the only place to read it.

## Wheels match the vectorscope

Each disc is turned so that a hue sits where the [vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/) draws it. Dragging toward a colour moves the trace toward that colour.

Red sits 103° counter-clockwise from 3 o'clock, just left of the top. Going counter-clockwise from there you'll find yellow on the left, green at the lower left, cyan near the bottom, blue on the right and magenta at the upper right. Every 75 % target on the vectorscope falls within 12° of its place on the disc.

## Reset the wheels

| To reset | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| One wheel's push | Double-click its disc. The puck returns to the centre and the wheel's brightness stays. |
| One wheel's brightness | Double-click its strip. The value returns to 0 and the push stays. |
| All three wheels | Choose **Reset** in the section's header, or right-click the wheels and choose **Reset to default**. **Reset** appears once a wheel has moved. |

Select the clips and use the wheels as usual. Each control writes only its own values. A puck gives every selected clip that wheel's push and leaves each clip's brightness and other wheels alone. A strip or a field does the same for that wheel's brightness.

The controls show the first clip's values. When the clips differ on any wheel, a **mixed** badge appears. One badge covers all three wheels.

With an action selected, a puck, a strip or a field sets the action's end value, and the wheels ramp there from the clip's own values. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).

While the action animates the wheels, a disc shows a hollow square at the start value and the puck in the action colour. A strip fills in the action colour from the start value. A coral mark shows the value under the playhead when it differs.

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.
